solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drunk bringing large snake into bed

parts.note: BED opens up to take L + ADDER
L = large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A drunk staggering home and dropping a big snake into the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Large is not describing the snake; it is its own piece, the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Bladdered is British slang for very drunk, from having a full bladder of beer.

indicators.note: something dropped in a drink ends up inside it

explanation.surface: An officer's peach slice plopped into a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: Peach is not fruit here but a person or thing that is excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal praise: a peach and a belter (British slang) are each a real stunner.

indicators.note: dishevelled hair is tangled out of order, so the letters are too

explanation.surface: Edgar Allan Poe looking scruffy and wild-haired.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous means writing fables here, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal reading: Aesop wrote fables, so he is a fabulous writer in the root sense.

clue.text: Key is with lock in Harrow

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone fumbling with a key and lock at Harrow school.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public school and a farm tool; here it is the verb, not either noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: as verbs, to harrow and to distress both mean to torment someone.

clue.text: Wave over ship in thrilling ride

indicators.note: 'over' means on top of, and in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a roller is a long heavy wave
a coaster is a ship trading along the coast

explanation.surface: A wave crashing over a ship, making for a wild ride.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sea voyage really is a thrilling ride, which masks the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the fairground roller-coaster exists to thrill its riders.

indicators.note: the answer can be seen inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Spotting someone's head in a chance meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Dome is informal for a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal usage: the dome is a jokey word for the head, especially a bald one.

indicators.note: the answer is taken from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A grim call to hang someone from the gallows a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: Hang is the definition, meaning droop, not execute.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the droop sense: a sagging rope or curtain hangs down slackly.

clue.text: Glance at youngster upset in disgrace

parts.note: to scan is to glance at quickly

indicators.note: to upset something is to tip it over, and in a down clue that turns the word upside down

explanation.surface: A child left upset and ashamed after a sharp look.
explanation.walkthrough: Only LAD is turned; SCAN stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a scandal is a public disgrace, the outrage over shameful conduct.

indicators.note: as if said in a report, so heard rather than seen

explanation.surface: A novelist who is new to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The spelling needs the novelist's extra E.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Graham Greene wrote Brighton Rock and The Third Man.

parts.note: the last is the only one left

explanation.surface: A family where the only son left alive has survived.
explanation.walkthrough: Survives is a verb here, and so is LASTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to last and to survive both mean to keep going over time.

clue.text: Dizzy Delia entertains me, offering drink

indicators.note: a dizzy head is spinning, so Delia's letters spin into a new order
a host entertains guests inside the house, so the jumbled letters take ME inside

parts.note: used as printed, placed after LI

explanation.surface: A giddy Delia hosting the speaker and handing round refreshments.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is only DELIA; ME goes inside the jumbled letters afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: limeade, lime juice with sugar and water, is one kind of drink.

clue.text: Sent abroad, former editor consumes wine

indicators.note: to consume a drink is to take it inside, so the editor holds the wine

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A retired editor, packed off abroad, drinking wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Former does not describe the editor in the wordplay; it is a separate piece placed before him.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: goods that are exported are sent abroad for sale.

clue.text: God having party back at home

indicators.note: 'back' means going the other way, so the party is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A god hosting a party once back home.
explanation.walkthrough: Back reads as returning home but only the party turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Odin is the chief god of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Pair touring Canada wrecked Bobby's vehicle

indicators.note: a wrecked thing is broken apart, so CANADA's letters are rebuilt in a new order
touring means travelling round

explanation.surface: Two travellers crash their police car on a tour of Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British police officer; a panda car was the small British police patrol car.
explanation.definitionFit: British usage: the panda car, named for its old blue-and-white livery, was the bobby's patrol car.

clue.text: Is much excited by total theatre

indicators.note: excited particles move about wildly, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the total is all of it

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by an entire theatrical show.
explanation.walkthrough: Music hall was the British variety theatre of the Victorian era.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a music hall was a theatre staging comic songs and variety acts.

clue.text: Mum clothes a nice man in purple

indicators.note: to clothe someone is to wrap them

explanation.surface: A mother dressing a pleasant man in purple clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothes is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose colour match: magenta is a purplish red, close enough to count as a purple.

indicators.note: something bashed is knocked out of shape, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A person hit in the legs.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder includes the word in, which looks like a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a single ticket, bed or item is just one.

indicators.note: something that spreads loses its shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Helplessness as a cloud of gas in space expands.
explanation.walkthrough: Spreads looks like a verb about the nebula, but it is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone unable to act is powerless to do so.

clue.text: Shakespearean villain one from that time

explanation.surface: A villain from Shakespeare's era.
explanation.walkthrough: From that time reads as describing the villain but is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Iago is the scheming ensign who destroys Othello.

clue.text: Chap to kill carrying large instrument

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it

parts.note: to do in is to kill

explanation.surface: A man set on murder hauling a big musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Do in is British slang for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the mandolin is a small stringed instrument of the lute family.

indicators.note: the fat holds the one inside

explanation.surface: A tenant seized by an overweight landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: in Scotland the laird is the landed proprietor, landlord to his tenants.

indicators.note: what you eat goes inside you

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, H

explanation.surface: A police officer tucking into horse meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse meat reads as one item but splits: horse is H, meat slice is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a chop is a thick slice of meat, usually cut with the bone.

indicators.note: to turn about is to face the other way

explanation.surface: Someone relaxed about a report of a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: Report is the bang of a gun, not a written account.
explanation.definitionFit: A second sense of report: the sharp bang of a firearm, which is what a gunshot makes.

explanation.surface: A Tory politician trying to rise socially.
explanation.walkthrough: Member is a limb, not a party member.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal reading of the social phrase: upwardly mobile means moving up, which is climbing.

explanation.surface: An Asian painter spending ages on a work.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s stands for is, joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an era is a long historical period.

parts.note: a crest is a ridge of a hill

explanation.surface: A bird displaying a divided crest of feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: Crest suggests a bird's head feathers; it is the ridge of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the partridge is a plump game bird of fields and hedges.
